standard_prerequisites.name: Equivalence through contractible fibres
standard_prerequisites.statement: A map is an equivalence exactly when each of its homotopy fibres is contractible.
standard_prerequisites.use: It converts the goal into the pointwise contractibility of the homotopy fibres, which is how the proof proceeds.

standard_prerequisites.name: Homotopy fibres of a map
standard_prerequisites.statement: The homotopy fibre of a map at a point of the codomain is the type of points of the domain together with an identification of their image with that point.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the type whose contractibility is established for an arbitrary point of the codomain.

core_obligations: Reduce the goal by the fibre criterion: to show that the map is an equivalence it suffices to show that each homotopy fibre is contractible (source line 485).

Fix an arbitrary point y of the codomain and use the assumed map from the codomain to the type of equivalence proofs at the image point to obtain a proof that the map is an equivalence (source line 486).
Read off from that proof the contractibility of the homotopy fibre at y, which is what was to be shown (source line 486).

proof_roadmap.step: Fibre criterion: contractibility of every homotopy fibre suffices.
Apply the assumed map at the chosen point and extract contractibility of its fibre.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author labelled corollary at source lines 481-483: if every point of the codomain supplies a proof that the map is an equivalence, then the map is an equivalence. The proof (source lines 484-487) is short but it is the reduction itself and not a pointer: it moves to the fibre criterion, fixes an arbitrary point of the codomain, applies the assumed map there to get a proof of equivalence at that point, and reads the contractibility of the homotopy fibre out of it. Which criterion licenses the reduction and where the hypothesis is consumed is the substance, and the statement alone does not display it.
